title: Building Production-Grade REST APIs with Node.js
excerpt: A deep dive into designing robust, scalable REST APIs using Node.js, Express, and best practices for production deployment.
content:
Introduction

Building production-grade REST APIs requires careful planning around security, scalability, and maintainability. In this post, we explore the architectural decisions that separate hobby projects from enterprise-ready services.

Project Structure

A well-organized Node.js API separates concerns cleanly: routes handle HTTP mapping, controllers handle business logic, services handle data operations, and middleware handles cross-cutting concerns like auth and logging.

Error Handling Strategy

Every route must be wrapped in a centralized error handler. Never leak stack traces to clients. Use structured error responses with consistent shape: { success, message, data, errors }.

Authentication

Use JWT with short expiry for access tokens and long-lived refresh tokens stored in httpOnly cookies. Never store tokens in localStorage.

Conclusion

Production APIs are defined by their failure modes, not their happy paths. Design for resilience first.
author: Vijay Kumar

title: PostgreSQL Query Optimization: From Slow to Sub-100ms
excerpt: Practical techniques for diagnosing and resolving slow PostgreSQL queries using EXPLAIN ANALYZE, indexing strategies, and query restructuring.
content:
The Problem

Slow queries are the most common performance bottleneck in backend systems. A query that takes 3 seconds under light load can take 30 seconds under production traffic. Understanding the query planner is essential.

EXPLAIN ANALYZE

Always start with EXPLAIN ANALYZE. Look for sequential scans on large tables, high cost nodes, and row estimate mismatches. These are your smoking guns.

Indexing Strategy

Create partial indexes for filtered queries. Use composite indexes in column order matching your WHERE and ORDER BY clauses. Avoid over-indexing — each index costs write performance.

Connection Pooling

Never connect directly from application servers. Use PgBouncer or pg-pool. Configure pool size based on: pool_size = (core_count * 2) + effective_spindle_count.

Results

With proper indexing and query restructuring, most slow queries can be brought under 100ms without changing business logic.
author: Vijay Kumar

title: Containerizing Backend Services with Docker: A Production Playbook
excerpt: From Dockerfile best practices to multi-stage builds and container security hardening for production backend deployments.
content:
Why Containerize

Containers solve the classic 'works on my machine' problem by packaging application code with its runtime environment. For backend services, this means predictable deployments across dev, staging, and production.

Multi-Stage Builds

Always use multi-stage builds for production images. Build in a full Node image, copy only the dist output to a slim Alpine base. This reduces image size from ~900MB to ~80MB.

Security Hardening

Never run containers as root. Use a dedicated non-root user. Scan images with Trivy or Snyk before pushing to registry. Pin base image versions — never use :latest in production.

Health Checks

Add a HEALTHCHECK instruction to every Dockerfile. This enables orchestrators like Kubernetes to route traffic only to healthy instances.

Conclusion

A well-crafted Dockerfile is as important as your application code. Treat it with the same engineering rigor.
author: Vijay Kumar
